question: How do motorist and cyclist deaths compare year by year in NYC, 2013 to 2025?

options.metric: Annual number of recorded motorist deaths and annual number of recorded cyclist deaths, each the sum of its killed-person column across in-range crash rows.
options.grouping: Calendar year and road-user type (motorist or cyclist).
options.reason: Absolute annual counts directly compare how many motorist and cyclist deaths were recorded each year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013–2025; annual peaks were 139 motorist deaths in 2020 and 31 cyclist deaths in both 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: For each full calendar year 2013–2025, this plots the sums of the motorist-killed and cyclist-killed fields across all police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crash records; the metric is absolute deaths with no denominator, grouped by year and road-user type. Motorist deaths were higher in all 13 years, ranging from 72 in 2016 to 139 in 2020, while cyclist deaths ranged from 10 in 2018 to 31 in both 2019 and 2023. This directly answers the annual-count comparison, but it does not estimate exposure-adjusted risk or compare deaths in other road-user categories. The check found 0 missing crash dates in the file, 0 missing values in either killed-person field among in-range rows, full Jan 1–Dec 31 coverage in all 13 years, and 2,132,218 in-range crash rows total; the year filter omits records outside 2013–2025, and we retained all in-range rows because none had missing values in the needed fields.

options.metric: Annual motorist deaths and cyclist deaths as percentages of their combined total, calculated from the respective sums of the killed-person columns.
options.denominator: Within each year, the sum of recorded motorist deaths plus recorded cyclist deaths.
options.grouping: Calendar year, with two shares: motorist and cyclist.
options.reason: Annual shares provide a clear comparison of the motorist-versus-cyclist composition independent of the combined total's size.
options.answer: This data answers only part of the question: cyclist deaths made up 9.1%–27.4% of the combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths per year, with the highest share in 2019; motorist deaths were the remainder.
options.interpretation: This answers only part of the question: it compares the motorist-versus-cyclist composition, but leaves absolute annual counts and shares among deaths of all road-user types unanswered. For each full calendar year 2013–2025, the chart divides the summed motorist and cyclist killed-person counts in police-reported NYC crash records by their combined total, grouping the resulting shares by year; the two shares sum to 100% by definition. Cyclists' share ranged from 9.1% in 2013 to 27.4% in 2019, so a 100% stacked chart is a defensible way to compare this two-category composition over time. The check found 0 missing crash dates in the file, 0 missing values in either killed-person field among in-range rows, full Jan 1–Dec 31 coverage in all 13 years, and 2,132,218 in-range crash rows total; the year filter omits records outside 2013–2025, and we retained all in-range rows, while the denominator intentionally counts only motorist and cyclist deaths and excludes pedestrian and other road-user deaths.

answer:
1. Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013–2025; annual peaks were 139 motorist deaths in 2020 and 31 cyclist deaths in both 2019 and 2023.
2. This data answers only part of the question: cyclist deaths made up 9.1%–27.4% of combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths per year, with the highest share in 2019; motorist deaths were the remainder.
